title: Reading the grid: how terminals turn pixels into legible text
stressor: multi-column layout, justified text with hyphenation, mixed heading sizes
notes: Self-contained single page, all CSS inline, no script, no network URLs. Designed for a 960x640 viewport (120x40 at 8x16). A three-column layout (column-count: 3, column-gap 28px, faint column-rule) with a column-spanning h1 and lede, and four in-column h2 subheadings. Body paragraphs use text-align: justify with hyphens: auto under lang="en". Prose at 15px/22px fills all three columns. White background, dark text. Prose is original, authored for the Nyala corpus. Whole-node visual fragment identities keep repeated rows in separate columns, so this fixture passes the default collision threshold at 120x40, 240x48, and 158x86 with cell 16x33 and needs no placement override.
paint_displace_note: Not applicable under the separate-layers model. The block forcing makes page glyph fill transparent, so screenshot.png contains no glyph ink for this fixture. PaintDisplacement measures zero runs and skips every run; a passing command exit is not placement evidence. The open overlay-to-bitmap alignment gate in docs/TODO.md tracks a replacement reference.
